meaning: MS C run-time error message table (R6000 stack overflow, R6001 null pointer assignment, ... , "run-time error "), terminated by id -1; ends at the BSS start 0xa524

name: g_bss_start
meaning: start of BSS: zeroed by crt0 (0xa524..0xbd3f) so every RAM global starts at 0; DATA.OVL holds zeros here (wiki "0xa530 unknown 0x1820"). Named RAM tables inside: 0xa9bd disk state, 0xa9fc monster-table backup, 0xab02 view tiles, 0xac64 view objects, 0xad14 light/combat map, 0xb11c OOL pointer, 0xb11e tile anim map, 0xb21e OOL buffer, 0xba14 combat roster, 0xbb14.. dungeon RAM bytes

name: g_cur_disk
meaning: index of the game disk currently required (0..5; 2 and 5 alias 1)

name: g_display_mode
meaning: 0 = text mode, 1 = intro/loading, 2 = graphics mode (affects how prompts are shown)

name: g_floppy_count
meaning: number of floppy drives known (2 once drive B is used)

name: g_disk_drive_letters
meaning: drive letter for each game disk, 0xff = not yet known (DATA.OVL initial 0)

name: g_disk1_drive_letter
meaning: g_disk_drive_letters[1]

name: g_disk3_drive_letter
meaning: g_disk_drive_letters[3] (Ghidra cRam0002a00b)

name: g_sound_enabled
meaning: nonzero = PC speaker sound on (toggled by a command, set to 1 by INTRO)

name: g_status_dirty
meaning: status window needs redraw

name: g_monster_table_backup_a9fc
meaning: copy of g_monster_table for the duration of combat (part 2 named slot 1 of it at 0xaa04)

name: g_monster_table_backup_aa04
meaning: g_monster_table_backup_a9fc slot 1 onward (base 0xa9fc; part 2 named slot 1 here) - copy of the monster table made by run_camp_scene (base 0xa9fc; 0xaa04 = slot 1)

name: g_view_tiles
meaning: terrain tile of each view cell (row stride 0x20); 0 = an object is drawn there instead (see g_view_objects), 0xff = darkness

name: g_view_objects
meaning: object/NPC tile (0x100-relative) drawn at each view cell when g_view_tiles is 0 (row stride 0x10)

name: g_light_map
meaning: RAM: in towns the light map built by rebuild_light_map (0 = unlit, else the tile); in combat (loc>=0x80) the 11x11 combat map (stride 0x20)

name: g_combat_map_centre
meaning: g_light_map[5][5]; 0xdc marks a centre object

name: g_ool_buffer_ptr
meaning: near pointer to the SAVED.OOL buffer (0xb21e)

name: g_tile_anim_map
meaning: display tile for each terrain tile 0..255 (identity except the animated groups); used by draw_map_view

name: g_ool_buffer
meaning: SAVED.OOL image (object lists)

name: g_ool_buffer_under
meaning: second half of g_ool_buffer: UNDER.OOL image (Underworld object list) written by main() after a game is loaded

name: g_combat_roster
meaning: combat participants: +2 flags (0x80 party member, 1/2/4/8 state bits), +3 party index or monster char, +4 monster-table slot, +6 x, +7 y (RAM only)

name: g_roster_initiative
meaning: roster +1: dexterity for party members, stat0 +/-3 for monsters

name: g_roster_flags
meaning: g_combat_roster +2 flags: 0x80 party member, 0x20 inactive, 0x10/0x04 (COMBAT), 0x01 charmed; stride 8

name: g_roster_member
meaning: g_combat_roster entry +3: party member index for party-side entries (monster type for monsters), stride 8

name: g_roster_slot
meaning: roster +4: monster-table slot of this combatant

name: g_roster_turn_counter
meaning: roster +5: 36 - initiative

name: g_roster_x
meaning: g_combat_roster +6 x

name: g_roster_y
meaning: g_combat_roster +7 y

name: g_dungeon_wall_tile
meaning: RAM: wall tile of the current dungeon style, set by DUNGEON_8ffe (md part 4)

name: g_dungeon_floor_tile
meaning: RAM: floor tile of the current dungeon style (0x45 or 5), set by DUNGEON_8ffe

name: g_tiles_patched
meaning: RAM: 1 when DNGLOOK applied driver_tile_patch(0); restored with command 1 after combat

name: g_dungeon_flags
meaning: RAM byte after g_tiles_patched: dungeon flags (DUNGEON overlay) (md part 4)

name: g_intro_flag_bb18
meaning: RAM byte used by INTRO (md part 4); meaning not determined

name: g_stack
meaning: end of the DATA.OVL image (file size 0xbd50 -> DGROUP 0xbd40). crt0 sets SP = 0xbd3e per the ROOT analysis while ARCHITECTURE.md places BSS+stack at 0xbd50..0xc53f with the stack top at 0xc540; the stack grows down from whichever top the loader chooses - leave 0x800 bytes above the image
